description:
FILED s533b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-03) from a requalifier-port neighbour probe (`local our $x` in a switched region); PRE-EXISTING on the base 4fb60297, identical after the port (the requalifier leaves the declarator token as written in both -- a decl is not a use; the wrong package comes from the `local our` LOWERING).

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; scratch/s533b/pr/K2.pl in the s533b worktree):

    sub r { package S; local our $lo = "L"; print "$lo|", $S::lo // "u", "|", $main::lo // "u", "\n" } r();
    { package S2; local our $lo2 = "L"; print "$lo2|", $S2::lo2 // "u", "\n" }
    package S3; local our $lo3 = "L"; print "$lo3|", $S3::lo3 // "u", "\n";

perl:  L|L|u / L|L / L|L
PCL:   |u|L  / |u  / L|L     -- SILENT WRONG in both block forms: the local is applied to $main::lo, every use reads $S::lo.

WHY (read, not yet confirmed by a trace): `local our $v` lowers through the v1 `local` seam (Pl/Parser.pm, the "Detect 'local our $var'" branch, #3240's sibling), which builds the cell from the package the SEAM's environment holds -- the section's package (main), not the block-level `package S;` region's.  A plain `our $v` in the same region is right (N1.pl).  The file-level statement form (third line) is right because there the section IS S3.

FIX SHAPE: the `local our` branch homes its cell the way the plain `our` lowering does inside a region (the requalifier's region package, or the binder's `our` binding's perl_package for the declarator token).  C2 (closing the text seam, `local` first) would carry it.


=== DONE (s535a) ===
(Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, resumed s536; commit "s535a D2: the package-region residues on the binder".)  Re-probed on 06a4b8ba first (s533c moved `local` off the v1 seam): still wrong (`|u|L` for perl `L|L|u`) -- the cause was the same as #4440's, not the seam: the `local our $v` declarator was left bare by requalify_home and so localized main::$v while the region's uses read S::$v.  FIX: the #4440 rule (requalify_home spells the declarator in its declaring package) + `_local_our_decls` accepts the qualified spelling (`local our $S::v` -> the cell of package S, name `$v`).  Probes d4422 / d4422b perl = tree (`L|L|u`, `L|L`), base wrong; d4422c is invalid perl (perl: "No package name allowed for variable ... in our") -- out of scope by principle 9.  Guard Pl/t/span-binder-01.t row 14 (scalar, array, an expression `our`; FAILS on 06a4b8ba).  Status left as it is.
subject: `local our $v` after a BLOCK-level `package S;` (sub body or bare block) localizes $main::v while every use reads $S::v -- silent wrong, pre-existing (the v1 `local our` seam homes the cell in the section package)
